notes.title: TOP DOGS TURF WARS: $5K PRIZE POOL
notes.content:
ASCENDANT is excited to jump into its first-ever cash prize event: Top Dogs Turf Wars.


 What you need to know
 What is Top Dogs Turf Wars
 Top 4 clans advance to Nov 22nd finals
 $5000 prize pool
 The top players in a top clan of each bracket qualify
 Starts Nov 8th
 Ends Nov 10th

Underdogs prizing

 Lower bracket prize pool
 Free-for-all format

Bracketing

 Tiered brackets for small, medium, and large creators

How to qualify/earn points/leaderboards
How to get started

 If you’re a Top Dog already, you don’t need to do anything else but play
 If you’re not a Top Dog, DM us and we’ll see about potentially getting you in
 If you’re a player this will tell you how to join a Top Dog clan


What is Top Dogs Turf Wars?
Before I tell you what Turf Wars is, let me fill you in on what Top Dogs is (because it’s important.) If you joined us back during Steam Next Fest, you likely joined one of the many creator clans available in ASCENDANT. We partnered with creators of all sizes from all around the world to put their name into the game and invite their communities to support them.
If you joined a Top Dog clan you would receive creator decals for you to represent on the back of a leather jacket or totally radical sunglasses. Once you did that, you would be thrown into 2 leaderboards - clan and global. Your clan leaderboard would show who in your clan was the most valuable community member based on kills, assists, and biocore captures. The global leaderboards would show Top Dog clans with the highest score total.

So what are the Turf Wars? Turf Wars is the competitive battleground between Top Dogs. Creators are now incentivized to not only try to reach the qualifiers, but they’re encouraged to bring in as many players as possible into their clan. And the best part is that this tournament doesn’t require you to be a creator to participate in the finals. Anyone can earn a spot in the finals.
Prize breakdown:

 1st place - $1,250 (each player: $625)
 2nd place - $900 (each player: $450)
 3rd place - $750 (each player: $375)
 4th place - $600 (each player: $300)


Underdogs prize pool
The chance to win doesn’t stop for those who didn’t make the cut (this time.) as we have prizes for the top 50 placements (5th - 50th). The Underdogs event kicks off November 22nd and ends November 24th at server shutdown times.
Underdogs will work differently from the Top Dogs program. We’ll be distributing prizes to the top 50 global leaderboard holders. Underdogs will compete against their Top Dogs as well to try and earn their spot in the leaderboard - a literal free-for-all.
These brackets will be managed separately from the qualified Top Dog brackets.

Prize breakdown (per player):

 1st: $150
 2nd to 5th: $100
 6th to 10th: $75
 11th to 20th: $50
 21st to 50th: $25


Bracketing
Here’s a breakdown on how brackets will work for Top Dogs so please read carefully on how this benefits both Top Dogs and clan members.
Tiered brackets (1-3)
The goal of Top Dogs is to empower creators with a game that will build community, relationships and the best fucking game possible (amongst many other verticals here.) our creator pool comes in small, medium, and large sizes, ensuring these creators have a chance at the prize pool. We will be putting creators in pools based on their ccv (found via sullygnome) so that way all creators in those pools aren’t going to be outnumbered by larger creators.

 Tier 1 | 1 - 25 ccv
 Tier 2 | 26 - 75 ccv
 Tier 3 | 76+ ccv


How to qualify / earn points / leaderboards
Competing is as simple as just playing the game. That's it. Lets keep this short and sweet.
How to qualify
Play ASCENDANT starting November 8th

 Queue only in battle of the biocores
 You will not earn any points in bot matches

The top players in a top clan of each bracket qualify

 Qualifying teams 4 teams total

Tier 3

 Top Dog clan owner
 Top 3 players of clan
 *2 additional tier 3 players will be able to compete in qualifiers

Tier 2

 Top Dog clan owner
 Top player of clan

Tier 1

 Top Dog clan owner
 Top player of clan


The clan creator will receive an automatic advancement to the finals. If the creator wishes to pass their spot to the 2nd highest clan member they are qualified to.

Qualifying clans will be announced as soon as possible - likely the next day.

How to earn points

 Biocore captures - 25
 Kills - 1
 Assists - 1
 Creators receive a 2x multiplier for all leaderboard contributions


Finals

 The Top Dog finals will be held on November 22nd.
 A total of 4 teams will compete against each other in a private match against one another.
 2 tier 3 teams
 1 tier 2 team
 1 tier 1 team
 Teams will play a total of 4 matches.
 Each match post-game report will contribute to scores as a team
 Scores at the end of all 4 matches will determine their placement.


How do I get started?
Top Dogs (creators)
If you participated in our Top Dogs program during Steam Next Fest, you should have received an email from us asking you to complete the Top Dog form, supply your logo, and get final approval from us.
If you have not applied for Top Dogs and would like to join, shoot us a DM on Twitter or Discord for a hook-up.
Clan members (players)
Whether you’re a die-hard community member or a general player - access to this tournament is as accessible to you as anyone else.
Step 1. Download ASCENDANT
Step 2. Complete your character onboarding (character creation, opening video.)
Step 2.1 If you’ve played with us before, your progress from Steam Next Fest will carry over to this beta, so ignore step 2.
Step 3. Join a Top Dog clan by pressing ESC. And clicking leaderboards.
Step 4. Search for the creator you’d like to support, or scroll through the creator list for a new creator you’d like to support

If you have any questions, queries, or want to find out more, feel free to reply to @AscendantGame or reach out to our Community Manager. You can also join our Discord for more information or to chat with our Community team.

	Semi - Corruptor now has a damage bonus of 73% (down from 88%).

	The base damage of heavy battle rifle ammo has been increased to 20.72 damage (up from 19.98).
	The Fall-Off stat for battle rifles has been made less impactful on a module’s score. This means that modules with this stat have either had their stat or their cost adjusted.

	The Light - Round Nose ammo now has a -22% Fall-Off (down from -15%).
	The Light - Stabilizer ammo now has a +3.3% Fall-Off (up from +3%).
	The Auto - Rapid trigger now has a -8% Fall-Off (down from 0%).
	The Auto - Ultra Rapid trigger now has a -11% Fall-Off (down from 0%).
	The Auto - Rapid Stabilizer trigger now has a -5% Fall-Off (down from 0%).
	The Medium - Gyro-Bore barrel now has a +8% Fall-Off.

	Similar to the Fall-Off changes, the Effective Range stat for battle rifles now has less impact on a module’s score. Meaning modules that sacrifice Effective Range are now a bit more expensive and those that improve Effective Range are a bit cheaper.
	All short battle rifle barrels have been made a bit cheaper, except for Short - Muzzle Brake.

	Short - Muzzle Brake has instead been given some better stats for handling spread and recoil during automatic fire.

	SLR Wolfshead now uses a Long - Standard barrel (instead of a Medium - Standard barrel).
	The headshot multipliers from sniper rifles have been reduced. Physical sniper rifles now have a headshot multiplier of 2.0 (down from 2.5) and energy sniper rifles have a headshot multiplier of 1.6 (down from 2.0).
	To compensate for their lowered headshot multipliers (which is a change primarily aimed at heavy snipers), some of the base damage values of sniper rifles have gone up.

	Light and energy snipers now have a base damage of 60 (up from 50).
	Heavy snipers now have a base damage of 82.5 (up from 80.55). Heavy snipers have also been made a bit cheaper to compensate for a relatively smaller increase in damage than before.

	Energy sniper rifles now have a 30% bullet velocity bonus (up from 20%).
	The Energy - Super-Heat sniper rifle ammo now has a 25% damage bonus (down from 35%) but is also a bit cheaper to equip.
	The Energy - Field-Breach sniper rifle ammo now has a 15% damage bonus (down from 25%) but is also a bit cheaper to equip.
	Cluster sniper rifles are now cheaper to equip.
	In light of the changes to sniper rifles, some weapons have had some module adjustments:

	Tyr's Hand now uses the 'Flight Stabilizer' trigger, so it has faster bullets and is more effective over distance.
	Cluster-Strike now uses the 'Acid Burst' trigger, so its cluster bombs do a bit more damage.
	Devastator now uses the 'Core-Splitter' mag, which gives it its lost cluster bomb back.

	The Cluster - Shock-Bomb sniper rifle ammo now slows enemies by 40% with their cluster bombs (up from 25%).
	The Heavy - Tri-Shot sniper rifle ammo now has a tighter spread (equal to the Light - Tri-Shot ammo’s spread).
	All sniper rifle cluster magazines are now slightly faster to reload, except for the Compact Injector.
	The Volt Flux sniper rifle magazine now deals 10% of the damage to deathbringer passengers (still 25% against passengers of other vehicles).
	The base damage of plasma rifles is now 19 (up from 17).

	All Surge plasma rifle ammo have received a damage penalty to counteract this increase, so their damage should be mostly unaffected.

	The base bullet velocity for plasma rifles is now 500 m/s (up from 400).

	Again, all Surge plasma rifle ammo have received a bullet velocity penalty to counteract this change, and will thus be unaffected.

	The values of Close and Long Range Bonuses for plasma rifles have been adjusted. So many modules that adjust these stats will have had their cost adjusted (cheaper or more expensive when equipped). 
	The Quick Charge plasma rifle ammo has been renamed to Fast Charge (to avoid confusion with the trigger) and had its long range damage penalty removed.
	The Flux Energy plasma rifle ammo now increases damage by 36% (up from 28.33%) and has had its long range damage penalty removed.
	The Condensed Energy plasma rifle ammo now increases damage by 36% (up from 28.33%).
	The Supercharger plasma rifle ammo now increases damage by 53.5% (up from 41.67%).
	The Unstable Release plasma rifle ammo now increases damage by 33% (up from 26.67%) and is also a bit cheaper.
	The Shield Burster plasma rifle ammo now increases damage by 24.33% (up from 18.33%).
	The Toxic I plasma rifle ammo now increases damage by 4% (up from 3.33%) and its cloud does 12 damage per tick (up from 10).
	The Toxic II plasma rifle ammo now increases damage by 8% (down from 8.33%) and its cloud does 17.5 damage per tick (up from 15).
	The Pulser Mk I plasma rifle trigger now increases damage by 8.5% (up from 8%).
	The Pulser Mk II plasma rifle trigger now increases damage by 15% (up from 14%).
	The Auto - Quick Charge plasma rifle trigger is now more expensive.
	The damage reduction to shields from the Standard - Shield Enforcer plasma rifle magazine is now 25% (up from 15%).
	Hailstorm now uses a 3x Holo Marksman sight instead of a 1.5x Holo Brawler.
	Some of the weapons you can get from earthtree scraps have had new paint jobs applied to them.
	The Gyro-Bore sniper rifle barrel has been given a new appearance.
	The Plasma Array sniper rifle barrel has been given a new appearance.

Movement

	The movement speed bonus when wielding a pistol or beam gloves has been increased to 15% (up from 5%). This does not affect movement in the lobby, which remains at a +5% bonus.
	Item based movement speed bonuses no longer apply to Biocore carriers, but they also no longer receive a flat movement speed penalty for carrying the Biocore.

Perks & Abilities

	The Automatic Ramp-Up perk now caps out at a 10% bonus (as opposed to growing indefinitely).
	The Metal Melter perk now deals 5% of the damage to deathbringer passengers (still 10% against passengers of other vehicles).

Vehicles

	The turret vehicle now goes a bit faster and does more ramming damage.
	The cluster cannon in the deathbringer is now affected by the same immunity system that cluster sniper rifles use: if a player is hit by a cluster bomb from the cannon, they can’t take damage from other cluster bombs for 0.5 seconds. This should make the cannon a bit less devastating when fired into tight spaces.

Lobby

	When logging in to a lobby, we will now place you in the same lobby as your friends (if there currently are any in a lobby and there is space).
	A new TV screen showing the current standings of the Top Dog event has been added to the lobby.

Customization

	New facial hair options have been added to the character customizer.

UI

	The mission progress screen after a match should now display which rewards you will get when completing the mission.
	Friend codes will no longer be visible when in Streamer Mode.
	The team information while getting ready for a match has been rejigged a bit in order to be more flexible with different team sizes.
	The matchmaking screen has received a visual overhaul.

Bug Fixes

	Using Escape to exit the matchmaking menu while in a party should now also unready you.
	The player controlled gorlizard will now have a full health bar when it’s on full health. It appeared as partially empty previously due to lowering its max health during the playtest. Its max health remains at the lowered state, just now has a health bar to match.
	The 1k Bomber mission should now correctly say that you can also heal with energy bombers in order to complete the mission.
	Fixed a few typos and formatting errors in vendor dialogue in the lobby.
	The ‘hide and seek’ pistol should now have sound.
	The ‘the Gorlizard’ and ‘Deathbringer’ titles should now be awarded appropriately from the Puppet Master IV and Bringer of Death IV achievements.
	The ‘Seeker’ title should now be awarded appropriately from the Collector achievement, as opposed to the Plaything achievements. Those who got it from Plaything get to keep it.
	The ‘Forest Power’ event should now be able to show up on the event screen at the start of a match.
	Corrected the icon for the Puppet Master achievement.
	If a teammate collects your weapon from the Weapon Replicator while you are disconnected, you should now still have it added to your unlocked weapons when you reconnect.
	The game log message should now appear correctly if an enemy steals one of your weapons from the weapon replicator.
	Healing missions should now also update when you repair shields.
	You should now be able to properly select the sixth consumable in the UI if you’re using the Extra Space perk.
	The interact message from possession the gorlizard should no longer get stuck on screen after you’ve taken control of the gorlizard.

TOTAL OVERLOAD EVENT: THIS WEEKEND, CHAOS GOES FULL THROTTLE!
Ready to absolutely obliterate the ASCENDANT universe this weekend? Good, because the Total Overload event is here, and we’re cranking up the insanity to max levels for the Steam Next Fest finale. This isn’t your average Sunday stroll - this is biopunk bedlam on steroids.

[previewyoutube=zoQhLKGXMqo;full][/previewyoutube]
What's NEW?

 The Underground? Oh yeah, you’re getting full access. No more secret spots, no more lucky few. We’re keeping this bad boy always open so you can get lost in its twisted halls.
 Game events are dialled up to 11: Lightning strikes, drones flying everywhere, locked rooms springing up out of nowhere, and hoards of Burrowers that just won’t quit. It's the kind of unpredictability that’ll have you sweating bullets while you strategize your next move. Good luck with that.

On Friday at 8 PM ET / Saturday at 9 AM Japan time, we’re hosting a VTuber event that’s gonna take things to a whole other level. So, if watching your favorite VTuber blow stuff up while mindlinked to a Gorlizard sounds like your vibe, you know where to be.

Grab the Free Demo Before It’s Gone
This weekend is your last chance to get in on the free demo before it disappears next week. Seriously, don’t be that person who waits and misses out. Download the game, log back in, and get in on the action. We want as many players as possible to break our servers and leave nothing but Gorlizard guts and Biocores in their wake.

So, what are you waiting for? Wishlist and download ASCENDANT! It’s time to squad up, bring your A-game, and blow this weekend wide open. Total Overload is waiting… and it’s not holding back.

Don’t forget to join our community Discord for all the latest chaos updates and follow us on Twitter to stay in the loop for epic drops, events, and more.

See you in Harmony!


Patch Notes - Mid Steam Next Fest, 2024

Events

 Map wide events are now much more likely to be active in a match.
 The burrower is now more likely to be active in a match.

Match Rules

 The underground will no longer be automatically sealed off if there are new players in the match.
 For the weekend only, the Gorlizard Control event will always be active. However, during this time, we have also lowered its health a bit.

Weapons & Consumables

 A number of changes have been made to battle rifles in regards to reducing the effectiveness of rapid fire builds, especially at longer ranges.

 All battle rifles now have slightly more side-to-side shifts in their recoil. Some modules increase this even further than they used to, and many modules that could counter this effect now do so by less. More details below.
 The ‘Light - Round Nose’ battle rifle ammo now has a -20% Fall-Off mod (down from -10%).
 The ‘Auto - Rapid’, ‘Auto - Ultra Rapid’, and ‘Auto - Rapid Stabilizer’ battle rifle triggers have had their damage mods reduced further and their side-to-side recoil variance modifiers increased.
 The following battle rifle barrel modules now reduce the side-to-side recoil variance by less: ‘Medium - Dampener’, ’Medium - Toxin Amplifier’, ’Long - Standard’, ’Long - Dampener’, ’Long - Gyro-Bore’, and ’Long - Toxin Amplifier’. These have all been made a bit cheaper to equip as a result.
 The ‘Heavy’ battle rifle stock now reduces side-to-side recoil variance by less but has been given a higher melee damage modifier.
 The ‘Damper Frame’ battle rifle stock now reduces side-to-side recoil variance by less but has instead had its pitch variance dampening effect strengthened.

 The ‘Light - Large’ battle rifle magazine now costs a bit more to equip.
 Due to the above changes, the V-Tech 12 has had its ammo changed from ‘Light - Stabilizer’ to ‘Light - Round Nose’ in order to avoid sacrificing too much damage output.

Other Updates

 The match intro video should now be less loud.

Bug Fixes

 Removed some expensive audio that could result in certain CPUs getting crackling audio effects.
 Fixed a bug that could cause players to be unable to access their loadout if they played their first match in a party instead of doing the tutorial.
 Fixed a crash that could occur when going off ladders.
 Fixed a crash that could occur when vehicles took damage.
 Fixed an issue that could occasionally result in the network connection timing out and kicking players from a match.
 Fixed an issue that would cause some Steam achievements not to unlock properly.
 Text chat should now always properly display [Party] when talking in party chat.
 Fixed an issue where certain interfaces could lose focus if you tabbed out and back into the game.

notes.content:
ASCENDANT is Crashing Steam Next Fest, From October 14th!

Lock and load, gamers! It’s time to strap in, fine tune your custom weapons, and prepare for the mayhem because ASCENDANT is storming Steam Next Fest! That's right, we're giving you free Open Beta access starting from October 14th, where you can unleash all the pent up chaotic energy you’ve been saving up while we’ve been sharpening our metaphorical biopunk blades (no actual blades - we prefer our carnage with bullets, baddies, and biocores) Plus, for anyone who’s played before, expect to see some… ‘scary’ additions, because Halloween has arrived in The Lobby!

Did Someone Say ‘New Trailer’?
Oh yes, you read that right, we’re delivering a brand new trailer during Next Fest - packed with more biopunk madness and ‘80s neon-drenched carnage than you can handle. Think of it as a sneak peek at the havoc you’re about to wreak - trust us, you don’t want to miss it.
For now, here’s a little teaser of what to expect… 

Fresh Meat, New Features
For those of you who've already dived headfirst into the glorious insanity that is ASCENDANT, we’ve got some epic new features waiting for you, because what’s the point of strategic survival if we’re not keeping you on your toes? 

 New Event: Fire Sale: All shops will offer free items for a limited time during matches. Players will receive a 1 minute warning before activation, which lasts for 3 minutes.
 New Event: Forest Power Plants: Special plants can be found in the wilderness. Destroying them yields power and potential goodies, with varying rarities affecting the loot.
 Match Modifier: Event Overload: Activates more events than usual during matches.
 Bunker Dome: Assault Variant: New dome ability that boosts damage for allies inside.
 Customization Options: New premade appearances, beard styles, eye colors, and charms for weapons.
 Halloween has arrived in The Lobby!
Updates & Patch Notes: Yeah, We’re Listening
We’ve also fine-tuned and updated the game based on your totally polite (and definitely not rude) feedback. So, if more balanced gameplay, smoother combat, and all the fun-size improvements that make your massacre even more satisfying were on your hit list, consider it done:

[olist] Map-Wide Events: Increased likelihood of multiple map-wide events occurring simultaneously!
 Weapon Unlock Changes: Unlocking new weapons now grants additional modules and perks, retroactively awarded to existing players.
 Boss Summoner Event Revamp: Now appears as a small camp with a console and a scanner drone, providing a clearer path to the boss after activation.
 Vehicle Update: The three-seater vehicle has received a new appearance, and you can earn and apply custom skins to the quad vehicle.
 Gorlizard Control Changes: Our big, scaly boy now has a loud roar when possessed, and when he uses any of his abilities (Roar, Leap, or Heal), it will also leave a temporary marker on the map, to give you a rough idea of where he might be!
 Lobby Updates: The pub has been renamed to The Side Quest and chat options for vendors have been expanded to provide you with useful gameplay tips.
 Deathbringer Clarity Update: Health gauge appears when shot; a ‘repairing’ icon is now displayed when disabled.
 UI Improvements: Redesigned accolade screens, longer chat window duration, and updated customization icons.
 Performance Enhancements: Various performance improvements, including clearer player outlines and projectile tracers.[/olist]
For the full list of changes, check out the Patch Notes.

ASCENDANT Is The Place To Be, From October 14th

During Steam Next Fest, you’ll be given full access to ASCENDANT’s world of retro-futuristic carnage. Our multi-team squad-based tactical shooter isn’t just about shooting stuff (okay, it’s a lot about shooting stuff), the name of the game is to adapt, strategise, and survive. Oh, and to make sure your opponents walk away with their dignity in tatters - while you claim victory with those sweet, sweet biocores. 

And when you’re not balls-deep in mutant turtle guts or dodging bullets from the other side of the map, you can head on over to The Lobby, where you can craft new weapons, battle with other players, run time trials, and even play hide-and-seek (you’ll see). It’s also a great place to trash talk while prepping your loadout for your next mission.

Wishlist Now, Play Later

So, what are you waiting for? Get yourself over to Steam and wishlist ASCENDANT now, so you’ll be ready to jump in as soon as Next Fest begins. We’ll see you on the battlefield.

notes.title: Steam Next Fest Beta Patch Notes
notes.content:
It's been approximately 71 days since our open beta in August. We've made significant changes to ASCENDANT that we believe you will enjoy. Please take a look at what to expect during our week long Steam Next Fest Beta.

If you require any technical assistance, the best place for support is in our games community discord. You can join here if you haven't yet! https://discord.gg/7jf6336X 

Events

	The likelihood that multiple ‘map wide events’ are active at the same time has been increased.

	For those unfamiliar with this term: ‘map wide events’ is how we refer to events that are automatically active and automatically affect the wider map in some way. For example, lightning strikes, locked main corridor entrances, central surveillance drones, etc.

	A new event has been added: Fire Sale.

	For a brief period during the match, everything in all shops around the map will be completely free.
	You will be made aware of if Fire Sale will be on at some point during the match in the event overview at the start.
	There will be a 1-minute warning before Fire Sale turns on, and it stays active for 3 minutes.

	Another map wide event has been added: Forest Power Plants.

	When active, there will be special plants dotted around the trees and cave walls in the wilderness. You can destroy them by shooting at them. When destroyed, they drop power and some potential other goodies.
	The plants come in a few different rarities, fairly distributed between spawning locations. The rarer plants (obviously) drop better things.

	A new match modifier (not quite an event in its own right) has been added: event overload. When active, loads more events than usual will be on in the match.
	The Boss Summoner event has had an uplift and been moved slightly. Chances are you never even saw it before, which was part of the problem.

	It can appear in two locations in the wilderness: in the caves to the waste, on top of one of the buildings between the forest and swamp to the east.
	It’s now dressed up as a small camp with a console and a scanner drone. It still costs 200 power to activate. After activating it, the drone will lead the way to where the boss will appear.

	The Upgrade Uplinks have received a face lift and now give out more information as to what they’re doing.

	They are still large satellite dish looking things on top of a couple of buildings in the shade, but now larger than before.
	If the event is not active, the device isn’t present at all.
	When under your team’s control, the display will also tell you which team upgrade it is funneling power into.

	It wouldn’t be an update without some changes to the Gorlizard Control event:

	When the gorlizard is possessed, a loud roar can be heard, to let you know what’s coming.
	The Roar ability sound has also been made louder.
	When the gorlizard uses any of its abilities (Roar, Leap, or Heal), it will also leave a temporary marker on the map, to give you a rough idea of where it might be.

	The Deathbringer has received a few clarity updates:

	When shot, a small health gauge will appear next to your crosshair (similar to that of the player controlled gorlizard) to give you a clearer idea of how much health it has.
	While disabled, it will now show a ‘repairing’ icon to more clearly indicate that it has been disabled (in case the smoke and fire is obscured by other smoke and fire).

	The uplift to the Weapon Replicator event that was mentioned in the last patch notes should now be in for real.

	It should now be much clearer when the event is active, when it is printing weapons, and when it has weapons ready and waiting.

	The screens on the Extraction Uplinks (big pylons in the wilderness) have been remade to be easier to read.

Match Rules

	Whether you won or lost a match is now called out immediately when a match ends, instead of having to wait for the celebration screen to find out.

Weapons & Consumables

	How Weapon Unlocks work has undergone some changes.

	Like before, on certain level milestones, you will be given the option to unlock a new weapon. This means that you will get access to all vendors associated with said weapon and can access it in the Weapon Customizer.
	Now, in addition to the above, each new weapon will give you more modules to go along with it, along with a weapon specific perk.
	Additionally, to save you some hassle, a new custom gun using your new modules will be automatically added to your list of custom weapons of that type and, if there is space, also added to your loadout.
	Any players who have already unlocked weapons have been retroactively awarded the modules and perk.

	The damage reducing effect from the Berzerk Boost plant now lasts 20 seconds (up from 10).
	Different beam gloves and energy bombers you can buy or find in a match should now have some different appearances to make them easier to tell apart.
	More weapon modules have received bespoke appearances.
	Battle rifle audio has had some minor tweaks.
The hyper cannon now reloads automatically on default reload settings (you no longer need to manually initiate it).
Hit marks should now appear when you shoot shield repair domes, healing domes, and lightning rods.

Movement

	You can now immediately climb after using a wind vortex or pulse bomb into a wall.
The amount of time you get slowed by after getting shot has been slightly increased. You are now slowed by 20% for 0.5 seconds, and it then dissipates over the 0.5 seconds after that. This effect still can’t occur more often than every 2 seconds.

Abilities & Perks

	The cooldown of the Thundercall: Sequence ability has been reduced to 45 seconds (down from 60).
	The cooldown of the Thundercall: Rapid ability has been reduced to 20 seconds (down from 25) and its activation time has been reduced to 0.5 seconds (down from 1).
	The Bunker Dome: Defence ability now has a 50-second cooldown (down from 90) but the duration has also been reduced to 35 seconds (down from 60). The cost has also been reduced to 1,000 Upgrade Credits.
	A new variant of the Bunker Dome ability has been added: Bunker Dome: Assault.

	Like its sibling, it also projects a protective dome around you when activated. This dome lasts for 25 seconds but all allies inside of the dome (including yourself) also deal 20% more damage.
	It can be unlocked from Marley.

	The Cheat Death perk now has a 20-second cooldown.
	The Ammo Specialist perk now also allows the user to carry 50 extra energy ammo.
	The Resilience perk now also reduces damage you receive by 50% while downed and holding a Biocore.
	The Toxic Transfusion perk has been nerfed a bit, and the heal now has a 1.5 second cooldown (up from 1 second).
	The bonus damage from the Cluster Splitter perk has been increased to 40% (from 20%).

Vehicles

	The three-seater vehicle (the one with a machine gun up top) has been given a new look.
	You can now be awarded with different vehicle skins that you can apply to your quad.

Environment

	A lot of new plants have been added to the wilderness.
	Some less obvious plant swaps have also taken place in order to improve performance.
	The ladder going from the cave into the exec quarter no longer has a hatch door, making it quicker and easier to get up and down.
	A lot of lighting around the map has been updated.

Lobby

	Halloween has arrived in the lobby! Not that anyone can remember what it is, but it feels right.
	A number of vendors have received more chat options.

	Some can provide you with useful gameplay tips, or you can chat to them for some more lore insight or just to get to know them better.
	More will come in future updates.

	The pub in the lobby has been renamed to The Side Quest. Gone with the Saucy Snail is also the strangely chested cattermaw. You will be missed (or, more likely, not).
The gun sounds from the firing ranges should be a bit quieter.

Customization

	New players can now choose between different premade appearances instead of being given one at random.
	A new beard style has been added. Hell yeah.
	Some new eye colors have been added.
	Face wear should now get hidden while you are applying face customizations.
	More different kinds of underwear have been added.
	You can now be rewarded with charms that can be equipped to your weapons.
You can now be rewarded with weapon skins that can be used to override the appearance of certain weapons.This only applies to weapons that can’t be built with modules (e.g. pistols and hyper weapons).

UI

	The accolade and results screens at the end of a match have been redesigned slightly.

	The result screen should now make it clearer where your XP and Credit rewards are coming from.

	The chat window will now stay open for longer after a new message has been sent or received.
	The ‘select your free flag decals’ interface now has a search field.
	You can now toggle off the health and shield bar numbers in the settings menu.
	Player stats that are given as ‘time spent’ should now display minutes and seconds instead of just seconds.
	Various icons for customization items and consumables have been replaced with updated versions.
Various UI effects and dressing components have been given a face lift.

Other Updates

	More improvements to performance.
	The resurrection point ping now lasts longer.
	Player outlines have been reworked to be clearer at distance and make it easier to distinguish if a highlighted player is behind or in front of obstacles.
	All projectile tracers have been completely reworked to be a bit clearer and also more performant.
	Fire can now damage doors.
	Some previously silent interactions now have sound effects. Notably, this includes a sound effect for stealing Biocores from a base. So you should now be able to hear if an enemy player is trying to sneak it away.
	Made some changes to how ‘shaders are being compiled’ is messaged to be a bit less jarring.
	Reworked how fire looks on players and creatures when they are on fire. It should now look less like intermittent explosions.
	More achievements have been added.
	More achievements have been given cosmetic rewards. If you have already completed such an achievement, you will automatically be given the reward.
	Your current state in game will now be shown in your Steam friends list.
	Updated various healing effects that were yellow to instead be green.
Leaderboard support has been added. For the time being, they are only used by the Top Dog event, but will be expanded to include more leaderboards with a future update.
You can now block voice chat in the lobby without also having to block team chat. Lobby voice chat block defaults to ON, so you’ll need to unblock it under Audio Options.
Rare dyes should now be a bit more likely to get from rare mystery bags.
You can now link your Twitch account to the game, in order to participate in Twitch drop events.

Bug Fixes

	Fixed an issue where a bad connection could lead to bullets not being allowed to register hits in close range combat.
	The Factory Printer event buttons should no longer claim to be ‘ready’ when the event is offline.

	They should also be easier to interact with when the event is active.


	Various collision fixes around the map, making collisions smoother and easier to traverse.
Some of these fixes will also have removed instances where you would end up briefly teleporting up and down at the end of a climb (e.g. on the cylindrical shape on top of the thermal transfer building).

	Fixed an issue where you couldn’t uncrouch if you were holding a Biocore and crouched inside a forward camp.
	More fixes to IK interactions with various surfaces to stop players and NPCs clipping through them onto whatever was beneath.
	Your arms should no longer be floating while wielding beam gloves in an ultra wide resolution.
	The hyper cannon icon has been updated to match its new appearance.
	Fixed some issues where the earthtree drop pods would reinitialise some effects if you disconnected and reconnected.
	The Long-Range Reinforcer and Headhunter perks should be working as intended again.
	The Shield Upgrader perk can now upgrade tier 3 shields to tier 4 again.
	The Metal Melter perk’s bonus damage to vehicles should now be working properly.
	Recharger modules should once again be able to generate ammo even while not equipped.
	Made some fixes to various hairstyles to make them fit different head shapes a bit better.
	Burrower pings should have their voice callouts back.
	The pick-ups for the Hyper Cannon, Hyper Rifle, Flamethrower, Surge Beam, and X3 Incendiary pistol are no longer just red.
	Level up effects should no longer be getting stuck in the lobby.
	The Gorlizard Control event now uses the correct icon.
	The Shop Uplink should no longer give out power twice each cycle.
	Banner parts that come from achievements should now tell you which achievements they come from, if you haven’t unlocked them yet.
	Fixed an issue where the scope shader wouldn’t go away properly if you Alt-tabbed out of the game while in scope mode.
	The ‘wall of fame’ display in the bar should now display all names correctly.
	You should no longer be able to make it into the water treatment room through the large pipe if the area is not available in a match.
	The ‘contesting’ overlay should now go away if you contest a Biocore as a gorlizard and then get killed and sent back to your regular, old human body.
	Fixed various overlapping elements in the HUD.
	Fixed an issue where cattermaw could get stuck in weird places.
	Tracker modules should no longer highlight teammates.
	Training dummies can now contest Biocores in the deathbringer.
	Revives will now get interrupted if you get knocked away mid-revive.
	Fixed a few dialogue typos.
	The spotlight banners around the lobby should now be better at displaying players who come back from a match with impressive stats.
	Fixed an issue where, occasionally, the ‘blur’ effect applied to the seeker in ‘hide and seek’ wouldn’t go away when the game started.
The Discount team upgrade should no longer require you to have the full cost power amount before spending the discounted amount.
Fixed an issue where the firing VFX could sometimes get stuck to an automatic weapon.
Traps can now be triggered by training dummies.
Fixed some doors that couldn’t be closed (they would just automatically reopen half way through the closing sequence, due to thinking something was in the way).
EMP grenades (and the EMP event) should now work properly with doors that are in the process of opening or closing.
Training dummies should now be appearing on the toxic gas and blast door maps.
When you buy a custom weapon during a match, only that weapon will be claimed to be ‘purchased’ on the little screens in the shop. Previously, if you had multiple custom weapons, they would all think they had been purchased.
When healing yourself, you should no longer see hit indicators as if you hit an enemy.

notes.title: Weapon Customisation
notes.content:
ASCENDANT.COM Weapon Customisation & More: Blow Stuff Up YOUR Way!

Gamers, are you tired of being stuck with the same old tired, boring weapons in every game? In ASCENDANT.COM, we’re basically handing you the keys to the armory and letting you go absolutely nuts. Want a sniper rifle that rains down explosive carpet bombs? Consider it done. Wanna turn your trusty rifle into a poison-spewing nightmare? It’s yours, baby. With our insane weapon customization system, you’re not just tweaking your gun, you’re turning it into a weaponized extension of your (unhinged) personality. From lethal efficiency to absolute chaos, whatever flavor of destruction you prefer, ASCENDANT.COM has got the tools for it.

We’re not just talking about changing your rifle’s color, no, no - this goes way deeper. ASCENDANT.COM gives you the freedom to create almost 3 million weapons, using our weapon modules. We've got it all, letting you turn even the most basic firearm into something straight out of your deepest, darkest imagination. It’s a world of carnage just waiting to happen.

No Free Lunch: Custom Weapons in Battle

As much as we love a custom killing machine, no one gets to start a match with them locked and loaded - that would be far too easy. You’ll need to earn your custom weapons in each match using in-game currency you collect while playing. So, if you want to unleash your masterpiece sniper-rifle-slash-bomb-thrower early, it’ll cost you. The more powerful you want your weapon, the more in-game dollar you’ll need to unlock it. Will you go for ultimate power early on, or pace yourself for the long haul?
And, like it or not, none of these upgrades carry over between matches, leaving you back at square one every time, just like every other sucker. 

Create Your Own Playstyle (Or Just Make Things Go 💥💥💥)

In ASCENDANT.COM, you’re not locked into being some generic soldier or healer, you decide who you want to be - mad concept, right?! So whether you want to be a sneaky biocore carrier with temporary invisibility and self-replenishing health and shield, or you prefer to just roll around with shotguns firing like a one-man apocalypse, the choice is down to you. You can customize your loadout with Biocore Abilities (powerful active skills), Perks (passive boosts), and Weapon Modules, to create a weapon that matches not only your outfit, but how you want to take out the opposition - just secure those Biocores!
Plus, if you’re new to the game, you don’t need to stress about being ‘behind’, as our progression system is designed to let you skip right to the good stuff.

Cosmetics and Trading: Because Looks Can (LITERALLY) Kill

Once you’ve built your dream loadout, it’s time to make it look HOT. ASCENDANT.COM is rammed with cosmetic options to style not only your character and weapons, but even your vehicles (coming SOON™👀). Customize the lot with skins, decals, and dyes to ensure your opponents (hell, even your teammates) not only run away in fear of your firepower but also envy your sense of style - because what says ‘SLAYYY’ more than an ‘80s sweatband, denim hotpants, and a leather jacket? 
ASCENDANT.COM is where creativity meets carnage. So, are you ready to craft the ultimate instrument of destruction? Get ready to show us what you’ve got.

notes.title: Closed Tech Test: September 14 Patch Notes
notes.content:
We've been grinding away at ASCENDANT ever since we received player feedback back in our August open beta, and we're excited to see what you think during this technical test.

After the event please complete our feedback form to let us know what you think. The more feedback we receive, the better and faster we can implement meaningful changes you want in the next event you play in. <3

If you require any technical assistance, the best place for support is in our games community discord. You can join here if you haven't yet! https://discord.gg/7jf6336X 

Performance
We heard you loud and clear, and we've made significant changes under the hood to meet your expectations. Performance improvements have been made in a ton of different areas. Like…a lot of things have been optimized. Loads. Many. Also Reflex Mode support has been added to the graphical settings.

Events

The poor Gorlizard Control just keeps on getting nerfed. These changes are primarily focused at reducing its survival and ability to play safely.

 Its Heal ability cooldown is now 120 seconds (up from 40).
 Its Leap ability cooldown is now 25 seconds (up from 20).
 The damage from its spit has been reduced by 20%.

Wind Vortices are now present in every match. Instead of just a binary ‘on or off’, different combinations of vortices will instead be active from match to match.


 Earthtree Scraps (the pods that can fall out of the earthtree) have undergone a lot of changes.

 They now come in two forms: regular scraps and golden scraps.
 Regular scraps always contain a tier 3 shield and power.
 The golden scraps now always contain a tier 4 shield or a team life, along with a special ‘beyond rare’ powered weapon. There are six possible weapons that can be acquired from the golden pods:

 T3 Viper - A semi-automatic spore rifle that deals triple damage with the last shot of its magazine.
 CFR Flamespitter - A pyro plasma rifle with a lot of self heal, and the fire reduces the damage output of any victims.
 HPR-200 Shellshock - A heavy sniper rifle with shield piercing rounds.
 BV7 Shield Breaker - A shotgun that deals particularly high damage to shields and comes with self healing and shield repairing capabilities.
 Grim Reaper - Dual purpose beam gloves tuned for both damage and healing, along with life steal.
 SF-10 Annihilator - A high powered energy bomber that deals bonus damage to shields with fully loaded specials and slightly repairs your shield when the last round of the magazine is fired.

 Additionally, there is a new match modifier that can trigger a rain of rare earthtree scraps in the early minutes of the match. Loads of powerful shields and weapons to fight over!

 The base chance of lightning strikes to spawn the Lightning Rod consumable has been increased from 5% to 15% (this chance still grows the more times lightning strikes close to any given team have not spawned a rod).
 The Shop Uplink event has been simplified and made more powerful. Instead of trickling out 200 power over time (with recharge times between each lots of 200) to whichever team controls one, 250 power is now given out immediately after it has been charged.

 The effect still cycles, so several lots of 250 power will be given out across a match to whichever team controls it at the time.

 An automatic Surveillance Drone event has been added. When active, surveillance drones will spawn from the earthtree and patrol the shade, looking for threats. Any player they spot becomes highlighted to all enemy teams.

 If destroyed, the surveillance drone drops one of the following: power, a frag grenade, or an HE grenade.

 As we are getting more of them, automatic map wide events are now more common.
 The Boss Summoner event now highlights the boss it has spawned to your team for 1 minute.

 This is just a little quality-of-life improvement for now; some bigger improvements to this event are coming in the next update.

 The Weapon Replicator event has undergone a bit of a visual overhaul and should now be much more obvious when active and when working on weapons.
Match Rules

 Mission specific world pick-ups and consoles now give score to your team.
 The match no longer abruptly ends when the final biocore is secured. This bit is still awaiting some additional polish, but it now announces that it was secured before the match results appear.
 In matches with a team size of 2 or less, and with 5 or fewer teams, all players will be given an additional life.

Weapons & Consumables

 Shotgun magazines have undergone some balancing changes in regards to their cost; i.e. by how much shotgun power costs vary when you equip different magazines.

 For light and energy magazines, any magazines with a ‘larger than default’ capacity have had their costs increased across the board.
 For heavy magazines, the costs of ‘smaller than default’ magazines are now slightly higher than they used to be.

 Shotgun blast pattern modules have also had their relative costs reviewed.

 The biggest changes have been done to the X and T spreads, with X getting more expensive and T getting a lot cheaper.

 Shotgun melee bonuses are now more expensive. I.e., shotgun modules that increase melee damage now cost more and shotguns modules that reduce melee damage are now cheaper.
 A side effect of the changes to shotgun modules is that the following shotguns have had various modules swapped out:

 Rigor Mortis (less damage and wider spread, but faster reloads)
 Last Horizon (slower reload but slightly more damage over distance)
 Oathkeeper’s Verdict (less damage and slightly slower reloads)
 Justicar (this one has undergone a much larger rework, focusing on fire rate over larger individual hits, and now uses the X blast pattern instead of the hexagonal)

 Sniper rifle energy ammo have had their bullet velocities increased by 20%.

 This does not apply to cluster ammo, but their bullet velocity penalties have been reduced from -12% to -10%.

 Most weapons you can acquire in a match have received new paint jobs. Beam gloves and energy bombers are still waiting for theirs.
 The hyper cannon has been given a new appearance.
 Some more modules have received custom appearances.

 Most notably is perhaps that the 4x Scope for the battle rifle is now actually a scope and not a holo sight.

 In order to improve response times when hitting a target, the client will now predict hits and show the ‘hit confirm’ indicator before the server has verified it.

 In general, this should make combat feel much more responsive. However, there may be some situations where the server can deny such a hit (e.g. if you happen to have had poorly timed packet loss or playing on an unstable connection), but this should be incredibly rare for most people.
 How much damage was done still won’t show up until the server has returned it, so this delay will still depend on your ping time.


Movement & Animations

 There is now an animation playing for when you interact with objects around the map. This animation is fully interruptible so will never prevent you from taking other actions.
 The crouched weapon stance now also applies to the pistol.

Abilities

 The Rocket Jump ability now launches you less far if you’re already high in the air when triggering it.

Vehicles

 The vehicle machine gun turret now has faster projectiles (900 m/s, up from 600 m/s) and tighter spread.
 You can now press Q to swap weapons while in a vehicle. The default button to change seats while in a vehicle has been changed to Z.
 Quad bike steering has been made a bit more nimble.

Creatures

 Black-red cattermaw will now drop a rare weapon if they don’t drop a shield (meaning you will always get some high tier equipment from them).
 Black-red and blue cattermaw are now a bit more aggressive and also use their ranged attack more often.
 Cattermaw projectiles now move faster and deal more damage.
 Destroying the neck gland on a cattermaw now deals bonus damage to it (as well as disabling the ranged attack).
 The entirety of a cattermaw’s shell is now destroyed in one go, instead of the two sides being independently destroyed. This should make it easier to take advantage of their weak spot underneath the shell.
 Regular gorlizard weapon drops are now uncommon instead of common.
 Burrowers always spawn in their unburrowed state, and won’t burrow until after they’ve been in combat.
 The health values of the burrower armor plates on arms and legs have been reduced.

Environment

 There are now many more respawn points spread around the centre of the map, and more of them will be active in each match.

 Remember that these respawn points can only be held by one team at a time, so enemies can steal them from you (or vice versa!).

 The Shop Uplink consoles have had their areas slightly reworked to make them easier to spot.

 For reference, one can occasionally be found in the admin offices on the surface, and one in ‘deep storage’ just behind the warehouse down in the vaults.

 More assets around the map have had their collisions reworked to improve traversal over and around them.
 The plants across the fields have been reworked to provide more consistent soft cover.
 The earthtree has been replaced with a new model.

Lobby

 The lobby has received more visual upgrades.
 New celebratory effects play when a particularly outstanding player returns from a match and ends up on the MVP podium.
 Some characters around the lobby have had some outfit and animation uplifts.
 A bunch of new hiding spots for the ‘Hide and Seek’ activity have been added.
 ‘ALL STAR’ displays have been added to the lobby, showing off creators who have met the requirements for the ‘wall of fame’.

Customization

 New underwear has been added.
 Some new hair styles can now be unlocked from Hugo.
 Celeste and Max have some new clothing items for sale.

UI

 More consumables have had their icons reworked.
 ‘Escape’ can now more consistently be used as a shortcut to close menus.
 The respawn screen now has named buttons to go with each of the unlocked points.
 Mission iconography has been updated to be more consistent and clearer.
 The customization UI has been updated to no longer be split up across three different screens.
 Health and shield values are now also shown as numbers next to the bars.
 The game log (i.e. the section where things like kills and team updates go) have had an update to make the entries stand out a bit more.
 The inventory screen has had some updates to be easier to understand at a quick glance.
 The ‘Winners’ screen have had some visual updates.
 Various buttons around the project have been updated to feel more responsive when hovered, along with some general visual uplifts.
 Some of the fanfare effects that appear when you, say, increase reputation have had an uplift.

Other Updates

 The smoke that comes out of a sabotaged base vehicle is now more clear and lingers for longer.
 Chip, the shop tutorial guy, now has an animation for when he’s sitting down and talking, so that it’s more obvious what’s going on.
 The tutorial video that plays in the cryo pod has been made a bit smaller so that players in tighter FoVs can take it in without having to turn.
 A greater variety of original music tracks have been added for those playing in ‘streamer mode’.
 Pinging a biocore will now also reveal it to your team on the map.
 The power pick-ups have a new model and there is now a visual difference between different quantities of power.
 The hit box for heads has been made a bit bigger in order to be more forgiving when trying to land headshots.
 You must now deposit power into shops before you can spend it.
 Made pick-up hit boxes for a variety of items larger; in particular for weapons.
 You can now be invited to a party (and play a real match) even without having done the tutorial. Playing a match with friends in this way will also advance the ‘do the tutorial’ mission so you can carry on with progression.

 You can still play the tutorial at any point via the matchmaking menu.

 The interaction area on the base vehicle sabotage point has been made bigger so it’s easier to interact with (e.g. to repair or use a hacking device to sabotage it).
 The intro video to the game mode tutorial has been removed. The information it presents is covered elsewhere anyway, so this should get you into the action a bit quicker.
 Different pick-ups now come with different pick-ups sounds (instead of a single generic one).
 More voice lines for picking up weapons have been added.
 Speaker announcements in the vaults should now be louder and audible from further away.

Bug Fixes

 A pretty big issue in regards to weapon tracers has finally been fixed:

 Up until now, all tracers have been visualized slightly in the past, meaning the visual of where your bullets are traveling is actually where they used to be and not where they currently are, which could lead to some misleading situations around whether your projectiles hit or not.

 With this fix, weapon tracers are now accurately representing where your bullets are traveling in real time.
 However, as a heads up, this fix has introduced a different issue which is still being looked into: when bullets hit walls, tracers can occasionally be seen disappearing right before the wall instead of on it. This is not nearly as bad as the previous issue, though, so we decided to put this fix in anyway while we’re working out the final kinks.
 NPCs in the lobby now blink. No dried out eyeballs for Victor tonight.
 Fixed various issues to do with some parts of the UI using default values if you disconnect and reconnect.
 Accepting a duel while you are searching for a match should no longer cancel the search.
 Initiating a climb at high velocity should no longer maintain that velocity when the climb finishes (and should thus not launch you into the air at the apex of the climb).
 Fixed a variety of snapping issues when going between animations.
 Fixed various typos.
 Removed a stutter issue that could occur when using a wind vortex.
 Fixed the upgrade station interaction text to not always claim they are unavailable.
 Fixed a few issues with the text displayed by mission computer terminals.
 Boss Summoning stations should no longer show mission markers when the player is on a mission to use them if they aren’t active.
 Fixed an issue where gorlizards would sometimes go through doors.
 Fixed some issues with how different modules made use of player chosen dyes.
 Fixed some issues with creature health bars not always properly appearing.
 A lot of little gaps between assets have been closed up. Mainly for performance reasons, but in some cases these were also large enough to look through.
 DLSS settings should now apply and save properly.
 The screens surrounding the airstrike console should now also be off if the event is off.
 The panels around the central extraction event should now also be off if the event is off.
 Driving over a wind vortex should no longer cause your character to look as it gets pulled out of the vehicle.
 The warehouse lift could occasionally break based on how the map unlocked. It should now always function.
 The objective description for the ‘Running (for) a Gauntlet’ mission should now point out all the locations where energy cells can be located.
 Fullscreen mode should now default to native screen resolution.
 You should no longer be able to enter water treatment through the large pipe with pulse bombs if the area is sealed.

We’re excited to announce the ASCENDANT.COM Insider Program. The Insider Program invites the most dedicated Ascendants and Community members to partner with the devs by participating in limited events to test updates to the game and to supply feedback. These opportunities are limited to players who register and are approved through our Insider Sign Up Form. Becoming an Insider grants you access to:

VIP Discord Server
Insiders will have access to our VIP discord server which will include direct lines to devs to supply feedback and to coordinate matches.
Weekly Playtests
Each week, Insiders will be able to choose what date and times they can participate in. These dates are highly limited and will not be on a build featuring any new content.
Feature Update Playtests
Play in major updates of ASCENDANT.COM. These builds will have more room/availability to play in compared to weekly playtests, and are expected to happen 1-2 times a month.

All community members are encouraged to register for the Insider Program. The Community Team will vet each form submission and reach out to approved members as soon as possible. If you are selected, you are not required to participate in every single opportunity. You will be asked to complete feedback forms that will be curated by our development team. If you are not selected, reapplying will not grant you a spot within the program.

Q: Can I stream or record gameplay?
A: Insiders are welcome to stream or record gameplay during any of the events they are invited to.

Q: Do I have to play in every single event I’m approved to play in?
A: No. Please let the CM team know if you are going to be absent!

Q: What is the goal of the Insider Program?
A: The Insider Program is a limited program for hardcore Ascendant fans to get a sneak peek at what’s under the hood, and supply feedback to our development team.

Q: Where would I submit feedback?
A: Insiders will be given forms per feature playtest. Additional feedback will be accepted in the private Discord server Insiders will be invited into.

Q: Can I opt out of the Insider Program?
A: Yes. If you are no longer interested, please do so, as we will communicate with Insiders in Discord and Email communication. We don’t want to bug ya!

notes.title: ASCENDANT.COM Playtest Overview
notes.content:
ASCENDANT.COM: Now in Color!

Welcome Convoyers, to the first installment of our DevBlog series! We are excited to share our feedback review with you. Earlier this month we held our largest playtest to date, and in this blog we’ll showcase a series of topics that we wanted to share regarding vision, outcomes, feedback and celebrate everyone who participated! Let’s get started!

Playtest Learnings
We’d like to thank each and every Convoyer who took part in our playtest and provided feedback. Your input is valuable to us, whether it was through our post game survey or our discord. The version of the game you played is still in development and we are constantly working behind the scenes to make the best game possible. During the playtest, we sought out key data and feedback to understand areas to focus on; everything from fine-tuning to rework.

Earlier this year we held a public playtest that was designed to tell us how effective we were in guiding players through multiple facets of the game:

 How do players learn the game?
 Do the tutorial missions achieve their goals?
 Do people pick up on what user interface elements are trying to convey?
 Do players remember what they have experienced in the tutorial and are they able to translate that into a match?
 How long does it take players to pick up on different aspects of the game?
 What turns players off of the game?


For this recent playtest we wanted to showcase the game’s largest art update and start to reveal ASCENDANT.COM’s biologically mutated and engineered world and retro inspirations. Harmony, the map you played in, is a beautiful place plagued with man made biological horrors and evolved abnormalities to immerse yourself in. With the beautiful and horrific art in place, we also wanted to understand how players discovered objectives and points of interest throughout Harmony. 

For this playtest, we wanted to identify:

 How does upgrading placeholder art assets with higher quality versions affect the player experience?
 How does a new tutorial flow perform?
 How do combinations of differently skilled players within the same match affect balance and enjoyment of the game?


What we learned was that the way we were teaching outside of the ‘game map’ wasn’t very effective. Not that it was a surprise, but it also confirmed our thoughts about what the impact of skill discrepancies between teams in a match would be and how this affects early player retention. We were also proven wrong in how forgiving we thought players would be of placeholder art (‘not at all’ was the conclusion). Despite this realization, we’ll move forward in making the game look even better the next time you join us. But for those of you who weren’t with us before this playtest, take a look at some “before and afters” of how the art has improved prior to your first time playing!

A Fresh Coat of Paint
The art of ASCENDANT.COM was a huge milestone for us to achieve with this playtest. You can see what our game looked like before we implemented many asset and visual updates.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43832685/e09a86dd088cf3207092225fc9a4a565698484bb.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43832685/c8d521f4654d640ae3f51c1e51915a3cc52ee7b5.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43832685/6aa649d43381325cd24db8e68849a926317b379d.png

You might have noticed that some assets around the map were still under development, but rest assured we’re still applying loads more into Ascendant each passing day.
Community Feedback
We put our ears to the biological waste ridden ground, spoke to the EarthTree, and had tea with a traumatized Gorlizard to understand what you had to say about your time in Harmony. After a few games of Ascendant we asked for your feedback regarding how your experience went. Thank you for spending your valuable time providing feedback!

We asked “What was your favorite moment or aspect of the game?”. Your top answers were:


 Gunplay
 No Fall Damage
 Character Voicelines
 Personality/World-Building
 Humor


We also asked “what was your least favorite moment or aspect of the game?”, so here’s what our lead game designer wanted to say on each to provide context on design direction:

Performance

We have very recently started getting art into the game map, so we are still working through all the optimisation the game needs. Hell, we haven't even finished putting the art in yet. There are still plenty of things in our TODO list here but we felt that the game had taken a big leap forward and wanted to share that with the community.

Tutorial

One of the things we want to avoid is holding players back for too long in mandatory tutorials that try to teach them everything before they can get into the action. What many of these tests focus on for us is effectively, "how little can we get away with hand holding players through, and what seems to be the most effective way of getting information across without becoming a chore?” A change we've made since the last playtest is that we effectively removed a "pre match tutorial" and instead try out a sample of other styles of introductions (e.g. videos, in-game hint systems, alongside the onboarding missions), so that we can see how this might differently affect how quickly players pick up on different things in the game. We are still going to be expanding more on tools to let players learn the games, and ways to more effectively convey new information, but it's also important to get a sense for which kind of tools seem to be effective before we invest too deep into fully fleshing them out.

Motion Blur

So what we're seeing at the moment is not Motion Blur but rather the result of TSR (Temporal Super Resolution). This is different from motion blur and occurs when TSR is not being fed enough data in the form of a combination of frames per second and screen percentage (3D Resolution in settings). 

What is TSR?

TSR is a technology that comes with Unreal Engine 5 and is similar to what NVidia's DLSS and AMD's FSR do, but with Anti-Aliasing included. The technology is still in the early stages but we're investigating solutions to the issue, including investigating DLSS and FSR. The main goal is to develop an heuristic to determine the appropriate Screen Percentage to keep TSR fed with enough data to avoid it looking like motion blur. Epic is also developing tech to solve this issue, and we believe that the improvements coming with 5.3.1 combined with our own solution will alleviate the issue. TSR is necessary when Lumen is active (High and Ultra settings on Global Illumination), we are considering alternative Anti Aliasing methods for when Lumen is off, and that would certainly solve the issue entirely. Keep in mind this was a pre-alpha preview, and investigation into possible solutions is still ongoing.

Movement

There is still more to do around player movement that we are looking to complete in the near future. This is tackled from a variety of angles: 

How the player character physically interacts with different types of terrain and obstacles when running, climbing, or sliding. 
How collision on obstacles is built to make the movement around these assets as smooth as possible. For example, avoiding annoying things players might snag on, uneven rocks that might be annoying to run across, surfaces that create jarring climbing experiences, etc. 
How the animations themselves play with the movement system. 

Across all of these factors we have polish to do. Part of what made some interactions with the environment less smooth than we want comes back to art: because we are still in the process of dressing the map, we haven't yet fine tuned all of the collision on rocks etc. This might sound like a simple thing to do, but assets on angled terrain or assets that sit next to or even on top of each other creates more variables that need to be tackled. A specific point on movement that came up with is in regards to how quick or slow (depending on which side of the fence you're on) the movement is. We are quite happy with the pace of movement as it currently is and have no plans to speed it up or slow it down, but we're rather focusing on making the above mentioned experiences smoother.

More PvE

More PvE will be coming but, to be clear, the game is intended to be a PvP experience first and foremost. PvE within the PvP matches will always be subservient to that goal and act more as side objectives or as interactive ways of collecting supplies. Once it is working as well as we want it to, we will be putting the rare boss back into the deadyard (some of you might've seen it in previous playtests, but it's not playing nicely with tech at the moment), but our goal is always for these more challenging PvE encounters to be more of an 'opt in' experience. We have a goal that we don't want PvE to create 'randomly unfair PvP encounters'.
Sensitivity Control

We have disabled mouse smoothing after the playtest. Mouse acceleration was never on in the first place, but it is something we plan on exposing for players to be able to set themselves if they so wish. Sensitivity sliders in general are getting a little bit of a change, too; we will be keeping all of the individual sensitivity settings but also create an ‘overall sensitivity’ slider that rules them all, for those who simply want to quickly adjust everything at once.

Beam Gloves are “overpowered”

Beam gloves are an interesting balancing case in that their effectiveness goes up in 'lower skill' matches but goes down in 'higher skill matches'. When it comes to the 'maximum output potential', they pale in comparison to all other weapons, but the question comes down to “how much of a weapon's potential can a player achieve with the alternatives”, and beam gloves, in the right situations, can act as a bit of an 'accuracy gatekeeper' ("if a player lands less than X% of their shots, the beam glove is a better option for close quarter combat"). When it comes to players with lower accuracy, we don't want beam gloves to become a weapon they feel like they "have" to use. But from the other perspective, we also don't want them to have too low of a presence in games with higher accuracy players. We have no 'planned changes' to talk about, but be aware that they are something we're looking at.

Controller Support

We can’t provide an estimate for when this will be available just yet, but ASCENDANT.COM will have controller support!

Radio Chatter
Some players even doubled up on their feedback after completing our in-game survey, leaving all kinds of feedback such as praise, critical feedback, and so much more. Here are some excerpts left in our Discord server:

"There is. So much to this game. I was nonstop discovering new features/enemies/map events/tech/mechanics. After the 4 hour playtest, I was kinda hooked. It's definitely the most in-depth pvevp game I've played so far." - [SF] BoboXXL


“The game is fast paced and very fun PVPVE. The biggest flaw in this playtest I think would be the lack of performance. Overall very fun game and fast pace, with performance issues as expected from a playtest.” - Kallliii


“Overall I would say its a solid start, and theres alot of room for improvement. Ill still probably play tomorrow, but I almost certainly wont be coming back for the next test unless the performance is improved drastically. ” - Someone


“I know there wasn't much optimization done so that was understandable, I think that should definitely be a priority for future playtests. Looking past a lot of the issues that can be fixed, I am really excited to see where the game goes. I've been wanting to get a game like this ever since the pre-frontier Cycle ended, and this has been the best one so far. Can't wait to see the progress you all put in, I can see and hope to see this go far!”  - Hekate (BocchiTheGosling)


“Overall the game looks better then it did back in April. But just feels unplayable for me currently. I'll check out a future playtest again down the line given the opportunity. Seems promising enough though all around.” - DKoi OP


We appreciate your time and value your feedback. It means so much to the team that you took the time to share your honest thoughts and feelings about Ascendant.

Would you look at that…

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43832685/b56ff1a43091f933ec39689452094ccd81e0dd7b.png
EPIC-HANDSHAKE.gif. Convoyers, it is with great pleasure to share that you do indeed got that dawg in you. Throughout the playtest you beat the hell out of every snail you walked across - you monsters. Speaking of monsters, 1.5 MILLION DAMAGE TO GORLIZARDS? You realize that they’re supposed to be threats to you, not the other way around?  We have more stats for you to flex on, so be sure to check out the rest of the playtest stats on our socials! 

“HEY I WANNA PLAY. OPEN IT.”

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43832685/476bcf09d23f87fa7be9f1bcbde6c3b7e66321ce.png
We’re extremely lucky and humbled to have such an excited community eager to play our game as soon as possible. Almost every day we’d get questions like “when’s the next playtest?!” Let’s cut to the chase - we’re excited to announce the ASCENDANT.COM: Community Playtest program!

Stock up on extra hard hair spray and get your montage playlist queued, because you’re going to need to look really good kicking ass! We’re working hard to get a date out to you as soon as we’re ready, so keep an eye on the ASCENDANT.COM Discord and our Steam Community page for the first playtest announcement!

Community Highlights
Our recent playtest wouldn’t be possible without YOU, Convoyer. Whether you are a content creator, hobby streamer or someone who just wants to make friends with snails, we’re beyond grateful for your support and participation. If you haven't already, scroll down to the "Join Ascendant Playtest" section on our steam page and sign up for the action. Already signed up? You're good to go!

Downloads and updates will be available one hour before the play test starts.
See you out on the battlefield!

Patch Notes

Lobby Activities
You can now play ‘Hide and Seek’ or duel other players in the lobby! You also no longer need to find a secret button to take part in the Rocky Road time trial.
Note that you can still queue for matches while taking part in lobby activities!

Hide and Seek

Every hour, a game of hide and seek will begin in the lobby. To sign up, head over to the back of the Drunken Drone.
If you don’t want to wait for a scheduled game, any player can also initiate a hide and seek match of their own, as long as it’s at least 10 minutes before the hour. To do so, simply head over to the console at the back of the Drunken Drone.
After a short countdown, one participant will become the hunter and be given a gun. Their objective is simple: find the other contestants and shoot them to make them join your team!
If all hiders are found within 5 minutes, the seekers win. Otherwise, the remaining hiders win.
The way to differentiate a player taking part in Hide and Seek from one who is not is that participants will not display nameplates when you’re close to them.

Known issues:

If you’re the first hunter and find yourself unable to stop moving at the start of a match, simply bump into an obstacle and you should regain normal controls again.
The hide and seek pistol is a bit poorly aligned, so will cover your crosshair when you ADS with it.
The audio announcement for a new match starting is not working, so we rely on you to spread the word when you set up your own games!

Duel Arena

If you walk up to another player and press ‘F’, you will be given an option to challenge them to a 1v1 duel.
Once the challenge has been accepted, you will get to decide on what rules you want to have for the duel, and which weapons you want to use (along with a pistol).
Then simply fight to the death!

Known issues:

The mouse cursor can go invisible when you appear on the rules interface. It is there, so you can still click buttons and it will reappear when you do. You can also Alt-Tab out of the window and click in again to regain the cursor.
Sound effects may sometimes get stuck when a duel ends.
Name plates will show up above your opponent’s head when you’re close.

Other Changes

Lighting and shadow settings have been adjusted to allow for better performance on older generation graphics cards when playing on lower settings, alongside many other performance optimisations. Note that we still have a fair way to go here, so all issues will not have been resolved yet.
The collision around a lot of rocks throughout the forest has been updated to make the rocks smoother and easier to climb, move around, and run over.
Text chat can now be fully disabled from settings.
The matchmaking introduction video has been given a new cut to reduce its length and focus more on just explaining the core objectives of the game mode.
Matchmaking will now take a bit longer to try to create more even matches before widening the search window to include everyone.
The ‘while waiting’ pop-up in the lobby now also instructs players on how to use emotes.
The screen percentage setting will no longer be changed by other settings when unlocked.

Bug Fixes

Friends on Steam will now show up more reliably the first time they enter the game.
Players should no longer be appearing naked at the start of a game while their customisation pieces are still being loaded.
The lobby now has a map that properly matches its layout.
Sound effects in the tutorial should now be properly affected by your audio settings.
Voice chat should no longer overlap introduction videos.
Various crash issues have been resolved.
Fixed an issue that caused the thermal transfer roof to be particularly difficult to climb onto.
Resolved an issue where a disconnected player would sometimes become invulnerable.
